description: Final polish - Settings page, responsive design fixes, loading states, error boundaries, and comprehensive test coverage. Ensures the app is production-ready with proper UX.
steps: Create src/app/settings/page.tsx - Settings page with sections: Profile (name, email from Google, avatar), Notifications (email alerts toggle for: trade copied, daily report, risk limit hit), API Connections (list connected platforms with status, reconnect button), Preferences (default risk multiplier, preferred timezone, dark mode toggle)
Create src/components/shared/loading-skeleton.tsx - Reusable skeleton loading components matching each card/table layout in the app
Create src/components/shared/error-boundary.tsx - Error boundary component with retry button and friendly error message
Create src/components/shared/empty-state.tsx - Empty state component with icon, message, and CTA button for when lists are empty
Create src/app/loading.tsx - Root loading UI with skeleton layout matching the dashboard
Create src/app/error.tsx - Root error boundary page
Create src/app/not-found.tsx - Custom 404 page with navigation back to dashboard

Add responsive design adjustments: ensure sidebar collapses to bottom navigation on mobile (breakpoint sm:), cards stack vertically on small screens, tables become scrollable horizontally, dialogs are full-screen on mobile
Create src/app/login/page.tsx - Dedicated login page with app branding, feature highlights, and Google sign-in button with proper styling
Add aria-labels, role attributes, and keyboard navigation support to all interactive components (dialogs, dropdowns, toggles)
Run final pnpm build and pnpm lint to confirm everything compiles and passes linting
acceptance_criteria: Settings page renders with all sections and controls
Loading skeletons appear during data fetching states
Error boundary catches and displays errors gracefully with retry option
Empty states guide users to create their first account/group
App is responsive - usable on mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports
Login page is visually appealing with clear CTA
All interactive elements have proper accessibility attributes
